commonQuestions.question: How much does this cost?
commonQuestions.answer: The founding cohort pilot programme is completely free. There's no cost during the 12-week pilot, and founding members receive lifetime free access if they continue.

commonQuestions.question: How much time does this require?
commonQuestions.answer: 30 minutes per week for family coaching session, plus ~1 hour per week for the young person. Much of this overlaps with existing activities - we're teaching them to extract more value from what they already do.

commonQuestions.question: Will this help with exams/grades?
commonQuestions.answer: The Voxel Programme isn't exam prep. It's about how you learn and creatively apply learning. That said, cognitive flexibility supports academic success. Learning about how you learn makes any academic effort more effective.

commonQuestions.question: Is this online or in-person?
commonQuestions.answer: Entirely online. No travel required, accessible to families across the UK.

commonQuestions.question: What age is this for?
commonQuestions.answer: Starting age 13-16, with 13-14 being ideal. But The Voxel Programme is a Consistent Companion - it doesn't end at 16. It continues with young people through ages 14-24+, evolving as they mature. Older members can become peer mentors or Voxel Guides. The relationship grows with them.

commonQuestions.question: What happens after 16 or after school?
commonQuestions.answer: The Voxel Programme is designed as a Consistent Companion that continues beyond school age. The programme doesn't end at 16 - it evolves with young people through ages 14-24 and beyond. As participants mature, they can transition to peer-to-peer support, become mentors or Voxel Guides for newer members, or continue as independent scholars. The programme adapts to changing needs rather than having a fixed graduation point.

knowledgeBase.title: Programme Overview
knowledgeBase.content: The Voxel Programme is a career navigation programme for young people aged 13-16 and their parents. It teaches self-directed learning methodology through the Voxel Loop, helping young people build three key assets: Continuity of Self-Insight, Personal Performance Assets (instincts, techniques, structures), and a Voxel Portfolio. This is not a course that ends - it's a Consistent Companion designed to continue with young people through ages 14-24+ as their needs evolve.

knowledgeBase.title: Founding Cohort Details
knowledgeBase.content: Founding cohort: 3-5 UK families with young people aged 13-16. 12-week free pilot. Lifetime free access if they continue. In exchange: full engagement, regular feedback, case study permission (anonymised if preferred), testimonial if programme delivers value.

knowledgeBase.title: Delivery Model
knowledgeBase.content: Entirely online delivery. Weekly 30-minute coaching sessions (parent + young person). All sessions recorded for transparency and safeguarding. Three support levels: Direct (coach-led), Indirect (email/messaging), AI-assisted (Voxel Hub in development).

knowledgeBase.title: About Patavox
knowledgeBase.content: Founded by Aran Rees. 8+ years experience in learning design and facilitation with major organizations including Hackney Council, TCS, Vodafone, and BT. Patavox means 'imagined voice' (from pataphysics + vox/voxel/vocation). This is Patavox - not Waycraft or Sabre Tooth Panda.

knowledgeBase.title: Age Range and Continuation
knowledgeBase.content: The Voxel Programme is designed as a Consistent Companion - not a course that ends. Starting age: 13-16 (ideally 13-14) for foundation years. Continuation beyond 16: The programme doesn't end at 16 - it continues with young people through ages 14-24+. As participants mature, their relationship with the programme evolves. Older members can transition to peer-to-peer support roles, become mentors or Voxel Guides for newer members, or continue as independent scholars.

good: The challenge is real - the career landscape your teenager is entering is more uncertain than ever. But that doesn't mean they're helpless. The Voxel Programme gives them the tools to navigate that uncertainty with confidence.

We're not going to pretend this is easy. Supporting your young person through this transition is hard when you can't predict what skills they'll need. That's exactly why we built The Voxel Programme - to give you both a way forward that doesn't require you to have all the answers.
bad: Don't worry! Everything will be amazing! Your teen will be so successful!
Your teenager is doomed without our programme.
